title: Eyes Up the Ribbon
hook: Deac has the wheel. The highway starts.
scene: Overcast morning on I-5 south of the Core. You are in the jump seat. Deac has the wheel, the thermos, and the log. The Ledger holds the right travel lane of three. He will name the interchange, the signs, and the paint while you watch. You do not touch the wheel until he says so. The mountain is a gray smudge far east. This pavement is the Ribbon.
debrief: You watched the highway before you drove it. Interchange, signs, paint, eyes up. Deac still has the next ramp.
ride_along: Eyes up. Not the bumper. The next sign. Then the one after that.
That stack of ramps is an interchange. We pick one gap and we commit.
The green panels name the cities. I-5 south until the I-90 east split.
Skip-dash is a legal change if the gap is real. Solid white is not.
Right lane dies into the next ramp. Through traffic holds left of that.
Count three on the pavement. At this speed three is a long piece of road.
Left glass. Right glass. Then the road. The box has no window behind us.
Do not slow on this pavement to read a sign. The ramp is where speed dies.
Someone is coming up the on-ramp on the right. We give them a lane if we have one.
Thermos. I drink when the wheels are straight and the gap is already ours.
You will take the next ramp. I talk you onto it. You do not stop on it.
Your wheel. Match their speed before you share their paint.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part one
source.teaching_target: Passenger-first highway observation: interchanges, signs, and lane lines before she takes the ramp.
